title: Bounded M5 bottom-series comparison (blocked candidate)
summary: Candidate private-input package for at most twelve frozen bottom series and three fixed 28-day horizons; no actual M5 input supplied or executed.
split_definition: Frozen at most twelve bottom series; origins d_1829, d_1857 and d_1885; next 28 days validate; all forecasts/scales/weights use history through the origin.
metric: mean absolute error (unweighted; not M5 WRMSSE)
environment: Declared target: Python 3.12.14 standard library on Darwin arm64; no actual M5 run recorded. Set private input/output environment variables as documented before execution.
steps: Supply authorized private sales, calendar, price and frozen scope files; inspect current access/rules and price-availability limitations.
Preserve at most twelve selected series, origins 1829/1857/1885 and horizon 28; compare unchanged seasonal-naive and four-week averaging forecasts.
Inspect every alias/origin diagnostic and retain zero-demand, undefined-scale/revenue and worse-method cases.
Compare notebook/script metrics exactly; keep the private series map and forecast/error rows outside safe-review. No full-hierarchy score or submission.
limitations: No actual M5 competition input has been supplied or executed; generated software tables are not actual-data acceptance.
Unweighted MAE and optional bottom-slice RMSSE exclude full twelve-level official WRMSSE.
Historical price publication timing is unknown; weighting requires an explicit availability assumption.
Undefined scales, missing prices and zero revenue stay explicit without epsilon or silent exclusion.
Private series identifiers and sales/forecast rows are not public diagnostics.
Traced allocations are not RSS; no actual learner compute budget measured.

project.outcome: Explain the same-method forecast comparison across frozen horizons and the limits of slice scoring.
prerequisites: Run local Python and configure private input/environment paths.
Explain forecast origins, 28-day horizons, MAE, scaled errors and revenue-weight limitations.

access.instructions: Inspect current M5 data/rules, supply authorized sales_train_validation.csv, calendar.csv, sell_prices.csv and private scope.json outside Git/public. Follow docs/m5-actual-data-setup.md. No automatic acquisition or submission.
access.authorization: Missing: no authorized learner-supplied competition inputs or access evidence received.

project.baseline: Repeat the last training week separately at each of the three fixed origins.
project.controlled_change: Compare the fixed average of four prior weeks on identical series, origins and 28-day horizons.
diagnostics: Do both methods differ consistently across all three frozen origins and selected bottom series?
Which slice RMSSE or revenue-weighted diagnostics are undefined, and what hierarchy/availability assumptions remain?
